jetbrains.derivefiles.smith-writes-every: smith writes every derived file that is stale or missing and records it in smith.lock. It leaves the files someone edited alone.
jetbrains.derivefiles.smith-overwrites-t: smith overwrites the file with the derived content. Your edit is lost; git can bring it back.
jetbrains.derivefiles.smith-keeps-your-e: smith keeps your edit as the new baseline. This works for a file smith owns by keys that still has every derived key. If the inputs change later, the file is in drift again.
jetbrains.derivefiles.the-file-becomes-y: The file becomes yours. smith writes "you" as its owner in smith.lock and never touches it again.
jetbrains.derivefiles.smith-gives-the-fi: smith gives the file back to itself: it shows the diff, rewrites the file and records smith as the owner.
jetbrains.derivefiles.say-who-owns-this-: Say who owns this file and why it is in its state. Changes nothing.
jetbrains.derivefiles.reclaim-give-it-ba: Reclaim: give it back to smith
jetbrains.derivefiles.every-file-that-is: Every file that is stale or missing
jetbrains.derivefiles.a-plain-smith-deri: A plain smith derive: it leaves the files someone edited alone.
jetbrains.derivefiles.derived-files-need: {size} derived files need action. Pick one. The first answer is the default.
jetbrains.derivefiles.by-default-smith-l: {effects} By default smith leaves the files uncommitted: review them with the Commit window.
jetbrains.derivefiles.is-done-commit-it-: {path}: {action} is done. Commit it together with smith.lock
jetbrains.derivefiles.by-default-smith-l: {effects} By default smith leaves the files uncommitted.
jetbrains.derivefiles.the-derived-files-: The derived files are written. Commit them together with smith.lock
